title: Fiscal Incentives for Medical Equipment Importation

qa_pairs.question: Which instrument marked the transition in legal authority for medical equipment duty assessment to the Customs Act, 2023?
qa_pairs.explanation: SRO 2025, issued on 2025-06-02, specifically cites the Customs Act, 2023 (Act No. 57 of 2023) as the legal basis for duty assessment.

qa_pairs.question: When was the duty reduction to 1% for specific medical equipment and supplies officially introduced?
qa_pairs.explanation: SRO 144-AIN/2022, issued on 2022-06-09, provided duty exemptions such that any customs duty exceeding 1% was exempted for specific medical equipment.

qa_pairs.question: What regulatory requirement for domestic production of medical equipment was introduced in 2021?
options: A total ban on imported parts for local manufacturing
Mandatory physical verification of production compliance every six months
Requirement to export 50% of all domestically produced equipment
Complete exemption from all taxes for local manufacturers
qa_pairs.answer: Mandatory physical verification of production compliance every six months
qa_pairs.explanation: According to the 2021-06-03 SRO, a committee must conduct physical inspections every six months to ensure that imported parts are utilized correctly in the production of medical equipment.

qa_pairs.question: Which instrument was issued in response to the COVID-19 pandemic to provide emergency duty exemptions?
qa_pairs.explanation: SRO 92-AIN/2020, dated 2020-03-24, was issued to grant emergency duty and tax exemptions for medical equipment to combat the global COVID-19 pandemic.

qa_pairs.scenario: A medical equipment manufacturer imported components in 2021 and is now planning a new import in 2025. They were previously subject to mandatory physical inspections every six months by a committee formed under the 2021 regulations to verify input-output coefficients. As they prepare for their 2025 imports, they note the shift in the legal framework from the Customs Act 1969 to the Customs Act 2023.
qa_pairs.question: How has the oversight mechanism for medical equipment imports evolved from the 2021 requirement to the 2025 regulatory environment?
qa_pairs.answer: While the 2021 regulation mandated a physical inspection committee to verify input-output coefficients every six months, the 2025 framework under the Customs Act 2023 introduces system-based audit requirements for compliance.

qa_pairs.scenario: An importer of medical equipment benefited from a full duty exemption during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. In 2022, they imported similar items under a new SRO that capped the customs duty at 1%. Now, in 2025, they are importing equipment under the new Customs Act 2023.
qa_pairs.question: Comparing the 2020 emergency relief to the 2022 and 2025 policies, how has the duty treatment for medical equipment changed?
qa_pairs.answer: The 2020 policy provided a total exemption from all import duties and taxes (CD, RD, SD, VAT, AT, AIT), whereas the 2022 and 2025 policies shifted to a standardized duty reduction model where customs duty exceeding 1% is exempted.

qa_pairs.question: In 2020-03-24, emergency duty exemptions were introduced for medical equipment. What regulatory change occurred one year later regarding the domestic production of these items?
qa_pairs.answer: In 2021-06-03, the government introduced monitoring mechanisms for the domestic production of medical equipment, requiring mandatory physical verification of imported parts to ensure compliance with authorized input-output coefficients.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2022-06-09 duty reduction to 1% for specific medical equipment, what significant legal transition occurred three years later?
qa_pairs.answer: Three years later, in 2025-06-02, the regulatory framework shifted from the Customs Act 1969 to the Customs Act 2023, which became the primary legal authority for granting duty and tax concessions for medical equipment imports.

qa_pairs.question: Arrange these events in chronological order (earliest first).
events_shuffled: Implementation of a one percent duty cap on specific medical equipment and supplies.
Establishment of mandatory physical inspection committees to verify the production of medical equipment using imported components.
Issuance of comprehensive duty exemptions for medical equipment to address a global health pandemic.
Adoption of a regulatory framework for medical equipment duty assessment based on the Customs Act.

answer_ordered.event: Issuance of comprehensive duty exemptions for medical equipment to address a global health pandemic.
Establishment of mandatory physical inspection committees to verify the production of medical equipment using imported components.
Implementation of a one percent duty cap on specific medical equipment and supplies.
Adoption of a regulatory framework for medical equipment duty assessment based on the Customs Act.
